title: D Norm
body_html:
D Norm

Let \(V\) be a right \(D\)-vector space. A \(D\)-norm is a function on \(V\) with values in the extended real line, allowing the value \(\infty\), such that \[ \ell(xd)=\ell(x)+\nu(d),\qquad \ell(x+y)\ge \min\{\ell(x),\ell(y)\}, \] and \(\ell(x)=\infty\) exactly when \(x=0\).

The norm is splittable if some \(D\)-basis \(\{e_i\}\) satisfies \[ \ell\left(\sum_i e_i d_i\right)=\inf_i(\ell(e_i)+\nu(d_i)). \] In the lattice-model sources, splittable \(D\)-norms are used interchangeably with lattice functions by the rule \(L_r=\ell^{-1}([r,\infty))\).
